d: Dynamic Clouds render realistic, customizable clouds that drift slowly across the sky.
h:
Roblox's dynamic clouds are realistic clouds that drift slowly across the sky. You can adjust their appearance through the Clouds object to create unique atmospheres such as stormy skies, stunning sunsets, and alien worlds. You can also customize their direction and speed through global wind.

Enable clouds

You can manage dynamic clouds in a game through the Clouds object. While you can place this object anywhere for organization or replication purposes, clouds only render if you parent the object under the Terrain class.

To enable dynamic clouds:

  1. In the Explorer window, hover over Terrain and click the ⊕ button. A contextual menu displays.
  2. From the menu, insert Clouds.

  1. Adjust the appearance of clouds through the new object's properties.
  2. Set the clouds in motion through global wind.

Cloud properties

From the Clouds object under Terrain, you can adjust the appearance of clouds through the Properties window.

Cover

The Cover property controls how much the clouds span across the overall skyscape layer from a value of 0 (sparse cloud cover) to 1 (full cloud cover).

<img src="../assets/lighting-and-effects/clouds/Cover-A.jpg" width="800" height="450" alt="Clouds with Cover value of 0.65" />

<img src="../assets/lighting-and-effects/clouds/Cover-B.jpg" width="800" height="450" alt="Clouds with Cover value of 0.8" />

Density

The Density property controls the intensity of the particles that make up each cloud, mainly affecting their transparency. For example, lower values produce light, semi-translucent clouds, and higher values produce heavy, dark clouds with a stormy appearance.

<img src="../assets/lighting-and-effects/clouds/Density-A.jpg" width="800" height="450" alt="Clouds with Density value of 0.05" />

<img src="../assets/lighting-and-effects/clouds/Density-B.jpg" width="800" height="450" alt="Clouds with Density value of 0.4" />

Color

The Color property controls the material color of cloud particles. It's important to note that several Lighting and Atmosphere properties also influence cloud color, so if you want to simulate specific atmospheres, experiment with multiple properties until you have the effect you want.

<img src="../assets/lighting-and-effects/clouds/Color-A.jpg" width="800" height="450" alt="Clouds with Color value of [255, 255, 255]" />

<img src="../assets/lighting-and-effects/clouds/Color-B.jpg" width="800" height="450" alt="Clouds with Color value of [75, 50, 255]" />

kid.simple: Dynamic clouds are real-looking 3D clouds that drift slowly across your game's sky. You add them with a `Clouds` object placed inside `Terrain`. Then you can change how much of the sky they cover, how thick and dark they are, and their color. They are an easy way to make your sky feel alive, stormy, or even alien.
kid.analogy: The `Clouds` object is like a weather dial for your sky. Turn up "cover" for a cloudy day, turn up "density" for dark storm clouds, and change the color for a purple alien sunset.
keyPoints: Clouds only show up when the `Clouds` object is inside `Terrain`.
To add them: in the Explorer, hover over Terrain, click the plus button, and insert Clouds.
Change how they look in the Properties window, then use global wind to make them move.
`Cover` goes from 0 (just a few clouds) to 1 (the whole sky covered).
`Density` changes how see-through clouds are. Low values are light and wispy; high values are heavy, dark, and stormy.
`Color` sets the clouds' color, but Lighting and Atmosphere settings also change how the color looks.
Global wind controls which way and how fast the clouds drift.

terms.dynamic clouds: 3D clouds that move and change, instead of a flat picture painted on the sky.
terms.Terrain: The object inside Workspace that holds land like hills, water, and grass. Clouds must go inside it.
terms.Cover: How much of the sky has clouds. 0.65 is partly cloudy; 0.8 is mostly cloudy.
terms.Density: How thick each cloud is. 0.1 is light and see-through; 0.3 is thicker and darker.
terms.global wind: A Workspace setting for the direction and strength of wind, which pushes the clouds.

watchOut: Putting `Clouds` in Lighting or Workspace and wondering why nothing shows. It must be inside `Terrain`.
Expecting clouds to move on their own. Set `Workspace.GlobalWind` to make them drift.
Getting weird cloud colors. Remember Lighting and Atmosphere also affect them, so tweak those too.
